UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION

MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE, Plaintiff, v. KATIE HALL, individually; NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN; META PLATFORMS, INC.; and JOHN/JANE DOES 1–6, Defendants. ____________________________________/ | Case No. 1:26-cv-02331

NOTICE OF WAIVER OF ORAL ARGUMENT AND REQUEST FOR PROMPT DETERMINATION ON THE PAPERS

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine waives oral argument on Plaintiff’s Motion Under Rule 26(d)(1) for Present Authorization to Serve Two Interrogatories on Meta Concerning Plaintiff’s Full Legal Name and Facebook Account, submitted on ____________, 2026 (the “Motion”), and requests that the Court direct submission and determination of the Motion on the papers under Local Civil Rules 7(E) and 7(J) and Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 78(b), consistent with item 9 of the Clerk’s Office General Filing Tips for the Alexandria Division.

1.	Plaintiff requests prompt determination upon completion of the briefing under Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1), subject to the Court’s directions. The present consequences described in the Declaration of Marvelle J. Ballentine, ¶¶ 8–16, and the access history described in Part V of the Memorandum in Support make the two limited answers time-sensitive.

2.	This waiver does not shorten any response period. Meta’s opposition and Plaintiff’s reply remain due as Local Civil Rule 7(F)(1) provides, unless the Court directs otherwise.

3.	[Record counsel for Meta’s actual position on determination on the papers, as stated at the November 9, 2026 conference or in the documented attempts. State consent or opposition only if counsel expressed it. If counsel stated no position, say so.] To the extent Meta does not agree to determination on the papers, Plaintiff maintains his waiver and asks the Court to determine the manner of submission under Local Civil Rule 7(J).

4.	The Court retains its authority to direct oral argument. Plaintiff does not request it. This Notice requests no hearing date, and it does not treat the Court’s November 5, 2026 entry concerning the motions previously set for December 16, 2026 as deciding the Motion.

Date: __________, 2026		                      Respectfully submitted,

Marvelle J. Ballentine

Plaintiff, pro se
